name: Chromeworks Silhouette SX-1 Stealth Leg
description:
The Silhouette SX-1 is a full leg replacement built around vibration-dampened ceramic-composite servos that operate below 18 decibels at all gait speeds, eliminating the mechanical noise signature that makes most cyberlimbs detectable in quiet environments. The outer shell integrates a multi-layer thermal masking membrane that suppresses the heat output of internal servo motors, reducing infrared signature to near-biological baseline, while nano-textured foot pads deform micro-dynamically on contact to distribute pressure and eliminate impact transients. The neural interface runs a predictive gait algorithm that pre-positions joints before each footfall to prevent reactive servo noise.

The SX-1 is officially marketed to executive protection details and licensed security consultants who require discrete movement in sensitive environments, but its real client base is an open secret. Chromeworks' sleek matte-black finish ensures the SX-1 looks as premium as it performs, which suits both its legitimate and less legitimate users.
installation_requirements: Full limb replacement, precision neural interface calibration required, Chromeworks-certified installation facility mandatory for stealth system activation
rejection_risk: Minimal — Chromeworks' proprietary biocompatible interface coating and seamless neural integration protocol result in industry-lowest rejection rates
maintenance: Thermal masking membrane recalibration every 4 months; nano-texture foot pad replacement annually or after heavy terrain use; servo damping fluid check bi-monthly
side_effects: Predictive gait algorithm occasionally misreads novel terrain, causing a brief hesitation stutter that users describe as unsettling
Thermal masking membrane degrades faster in high-humidity environments, requiring more frequent recalibration
Near-silent operation means users lose the unconscious auditory feedback cues that help regulate pace, leading to proprioceptive adjustment period of 2-3 weeks
Black-market activation of full stealth mode without Chromeworks certification has caused servo synchronization failures in 6% of unauthorized units
cultural_context: The SX-1 is the cyberlimb equivalent of a suppressed firearm — its purpose is obvious regardless of what the marketing says. In Tier 4-5 circles, owning a pair is a quiet signal of access to a particular kind of work or a particular kind of danger.
known_users: Licensed executive protection and security consultants
Tier 4-5 individuals with sensitive personal security concerns
story_hooks: A Spire executive was assassinated in a secure room with no entry logs — the only explanation is SX-1 legs bypassing the acoustic intrusion sensors, and Chromeworks' installation records are the only lead
A black-market SX-1 activation kit is circulating in the Undercity, and someone with newly silenced steps has been moving through places they shouldn't be able to reach
Chromeworks' certification facility has a side business selling stealth-mode unlock codes to anyone who can pay — someone inside wants to blow the whistle but needs protection first
